task_instance: In a fresh sample git repo (with a Python module and a test), detect that we're in a normal (non-worktree) checkout, create a .worktrees/ directory, verify/add it to .gitignore, create an isolated worktree with `git worktree add .worktrees/feature/add-multiply -b feature/add-multiply`, run the baseline test suite in the new worktree, then make and commit a change (adding a multiply() function) inside the worktree, and verify the change is isolated from the main checkout's branch.
evidence: Created sample-repo at /tmp/.../exec/obra__superpowers__using-git-worktrees/sample-repo with README.md, src/app.py (add()), test_app.py. Step 0 detection: git rev-parse --git-dir == --git-common-dir (.git == .git) confirmed a normal checkout, not already a worktree. Step 1b fallback used since no native worktree tool exists in this shell context: added '.worktrees/' to .gitignore and committed it (commit 5bfcb44), then ran `git worktree add .worktrees/feature/add-multiply -b feature/add-multiply`, which succeeded ('Preparing worktree (new branch feature/add-multiply)'). `git worktree list` showed two linked checkouts on branches master and feature/add-multiply at the same commit. Inside the worktree, GIT_DIR (.../sample-repo/.git/worktrees/add-multiply) != GIT_COMMON (.../sample-repo/.git), confirming true isolation per the skill's Step 0 check. Step 2: no package.json/Cargo.toml/requirements.txt present, so dependency install was correctly skipped. Step 3: ran `python3 -m pytest test_app.py -q` in the worktree -> '1 passed in 0.64s', confirming a clean baseline. Then added a multiply() function to src/app.py inside the worktree and committed it (commit 8f6938e on feature/add-multiply). Verified isolation by returning to the main sample-repo checkout: `git log --oneline -3` there still showed only the Initial commit and the .gitignore commit (no multiply commit), and `cat src/app.py` in the main checkout showed only add(), proving the worktree's changes did not leak into the original branch/checkout. This fully exercises and verifies the skill's core deliverable: an isolated, working git worktree for feature development.
